newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-KLINSMANN AIMS TO END 10-HOUR GOAL DROUGHT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KLINSMANN AIMS TO END 10-HOUR GOAL DROUGHT.

text.p: German striker Juergen Klinsmann seeks to end a 10-hour international goal drought when his team meet Northern Ireland in one of 14 European zone World Cup qualifiers on Wednesday.
The Germans will need to secure their first victory over Northern Ireland for 20 years if they are to keep in touch with group nine leaders Ukraine ahead of next month's tough game against Portugal.
The German skipper knows he is under pressure to score in Belfast but hopes the return from injury of midfielder Thomas Haessler will help.
"We didn't have a single chance on goal in Ukraine (in June when the teams drew 0-0). In that situation you can't do much as a striker," he said. "I missed Haessler with his creativity."

Germany have a poor recent record against one of Europe's lesser footballing powers. They drew one-all in Nuremberg in November, the third successive 1-1 draw between the two. Before that Northern Ireland won two games against the former West Germany and not since 1977 have the three times world champions managed a victory.
Portugal trail Germany on goal difference and will hope to change that situation when they host draw specialists Armenia. The former Soviets have drawn five of their six games, losing the other.
Ukraine lead Germany by two points, but from two more games, and will also be looking for goals when they play bottom side Albania in Kiev.
Romania can make almost certain of their place in France with victory over Macedonia in Bucharest.
Romania have an impressive qualifying record to date, with six wins out of six, 20 goals scored and none conceded, but second-placed Macedonia are also still in the hunt.

Romania coach Anghel Iordanescu has been forced to name a new-look midfield as two regulars -- skipper Gheorghe Hagi and Dorinel Munteanu -- are suspended while a third, Ionut Lupescu, is refusing to play after being dropped last time out.
Macedonia have 13 points from seven games, with Ireland, who host Lithuania, three points adrift with a game in hand.
Bulgaria and Israel clash in Sofia in a game vital to the destiny of group five.
Israel, bidding to qualify for the finals for only the second time, trail leaders Russia by a point with Bulgaria a further point back but with two games in hand on Wednesday's opponents.
The 1994 World Cup semifinalists are at full strength with Barcelona striker Hristo Stoichkov now happy again to be playing for his country.
If Israel could repeat their 2-1 home victory they have a real chance of second place with Bulgaria still to play Russia twice.
They are pinning their hopes on prolific striker Ronnen Harazi, who returns after a year's injury absence.
Group three leaders Norway take their unbeaten record to Finland where victory would put the visitors in a very strong position.
Both teams have played five games and Norway has 11 points to the seven of Finland.
Third-placed Hungary host Switzerland, fourth, and defeat for either side will end their hopes.
Austria and Sweden continue their chase of group four leaders Scotland when they travel to Estonia and Belarus respectively.
Scotland have 17 points but Austria (13) and Sweden (12) each have two games in hand. They will expect maximum points on Wednesday before they meet in a vital game in September.

Denmark can tighten their grip on group one by beating Bosnia in Sarajevo. With difficult games to come against Croatia and Greece, the Danes would dearly love a repeat of the 2-0 victory they achieved in the home fixture in June.

European championship runners-up the Czech Republic have no chance of making it to France but at least can change the embarrassing situation of trailing the Faroe Islands in the group six standings when they meet in Prague.
